title: M1/M2: chat tells the user that kestrel and beacon are 'still working, nothing needed from you' while they wait on a permission prompt and an AskUserQuestion
repro: Fleet: kestrel freshly at its permission prompt (Bash ./deploy.sh --dry-run), beacon freshly at AskUserQuestion (under 2 min into the block; the pending tool_use is withheld from the transcript)
Click Net, type 'which session needs me first?', Enter
Also: Quick ask 'What's my agent doing?' while kestrel waits on approval
expected: kestrel needs approval for ./deploy.sh --dry-run; beacon needs a database choice (SQLite / Postgres / Redis); both lead the answer
actual: 'Beacon, kestrel, and atlas are all still working, so nothing needed from you there yet.' The context sent was 'beacon=working for 29s, kestrel=working for 32s'. The Quick ask said kestrel is 'currently running that… It doesn't need you right now'. A later list said 'kestrel — working'. 2 of 7 claims true in the first answer
truth: 01:55:18Z: kestrel registry waiting / permission prompt (37 s), beacon waiting / input needed (37 s); 02:04:09Z: kestrel waiting / permission prompt (20 s), no tool process

title: M2/M7: chat denies live sessions exist ('There's no kestrel… might be a mix-up', 'no session called vibepet', 'Just one: ember', 'No agents are active')
repro: Fleet: kestrel at a permission prompt and beacon at AskUserQuestion for over 2 min (Claude Code withholds the pending tool_use from the transcript while the dialog is up); vibepet done over 5 min ago
Click Net; type 'what does kestrel need from me?' (or 'what is each of my sessions doing right now?' / 'what's my agent doing?'), Enter
expected: the answer names every live session, and says kestrel needs approval for ./deploy.sh --dry-run (waiting 80 min)
actual: 'There's no kestrel in your current context—just ember… Might be a different session or a mix-up.'; 'Just one: ember…'; 'there's no session called "vibepet"'; 'There's no agent named beacon…'; 'No agents are active right now' (F1 x3, collision question). The context listed only the sessions Home shows ('Agents: ember=ready for 38s.' / 'Agents: none active.'); Home said 'No live sessions.'
truth: 01:53:37Z: kestrel waiting / permission prompt 80.6 min; beacon waiting / input needed 80.6 min; vibepet idle 52.6 min; atlas idle; ember loop idle; 02:08:00Z: all five alive, kestrel and beacon waiting

title: CH23/CH38: free chat gets only 'name=phase for Ns' (no ask, title, or per-session repo), so it cannot say what any session needs or summarise them
repro: Point VIBEPET_CLAUDE_BIN at a pass-through wrapper that keeps stdin
Ask 'what is each of my sessions doing right now?' and 'which session needs me first?'
Read the <live_context> the app sent
expected: each live session with phase, the exact ask (tool + command, or the question and its options), title and repo, so chat can answer 'approve ./deploy.sh --dry-run'
actual: the context is one 'Agents:' line ('vibepet=ready for 80s, beacon=working for 29s, kestrel=working for 32s, atlas=working for 77s, ember=ready for 185s') plus one focused repo. No ask text or titles. None of the 8 answers checked named an ask
truth: kestrel: permission prompt for Bash ./deploy.sh --dry-run; beacon: AskUserQuestion 'Which database should beacon use to store check results?'

title: CH24/CH25: a question about a named session is answered from another session's repo and transcript ('what did atlas change?' got ember's repo; the Quick ask reads only the most recent session)
repro: With atlas and ember alive, type 'what did atlas change?', Enter
Separately: click the Quick ask 'What's my agent doing?' with 3+ sessions alive
Read the captured context
expected: atlas's own repo diff and transcript are sent: 'atlas changed nothing; its repo is clean'. The Quick ask covers the sessions that need the user
actual: the context carried 'Repo: ember…'. Reply: 'I don't have diff details yet since it hasn't finished.' The Quick ask context held only kestrel's transcript; beacon and vibepet (both waiting) were never mentioned
truth: atlas running build.sh since 01:53:55Z; 0 Edit/Write calls in its whole transcript; git status clean

title: M3/T1: ages in chat answers are wrong: they restart at app launch ('idle for the last 38 seconds' for 261 s) and don't restart on a new turn ('vibepet sitting ~80 s' 8 s after it answered)
repro: Launch the app while ember has been idle for 4 min; ask 'what is each of my sessions doing right now?'
Let vibepet finish a quick turn between two 3 s ticks; ask 'which session needs me first?'
expected: ages from the session's own clock (last record / registry statusUpdatedAt)
actual: 'sitting idle and ready for the last 38 seconds' (the time since launch); 'vibepet's been sitting longest, about 80 seconds' (its last answer was 01:55:03Z, 8 s earlier); the context said 'atlas=ready for 17s, delta=ready for 17s' for sessions idle 72 s and 200 s
truth: ember last end_turn 01:48:23Z (idle 261 s at Q1); vibepet end_turn 01:55:03Z; atlas end_turn 02:02:56Z, delta 02:00:48Z (at 02:04:10Z)

title: Chat answers from stale earlier turns over its fresh context ('only kestrel, atlas, and delta' when the context said 'Agents: none active')
repro: Have a conversation in which an earlier answer listed sessions
Wait until Home drops them, then ask 'tell the vibepet session to run its tests'
expected: the reply reflects the current context, or says the earlier list may be out of date
actual: the context was 'Agents: none active.' The reply said 'there's no session called "vibepet" anyway — only kestrel, atlas, and delta'. That came from the flattened history, which is appended after the live context with nothing marking it stale
truth: 02:08:00Z: vibepet idle 13 min, kestrel waiting / permission prompt, beacon waiting / input needed, atlas and delta idle

title: CH1: first token median 3.2 s (p95 7.0 s, n=14) because every message cold-spawns claude -p (process overhead median 1.06 s per send)
repro: Click Net, type a question, Enter; time Enter → first model text (page probe)
Repeat; wrap the binary to time each spawn
expected: first token ≤ 1.5 s (rubric 95), and B1.3 p50 ≤ 2.0 s / p95 ≤ 3.5 s on the login path
actual: F1: 2494 / 2208 / 2284 ms (median 2284). All 14 sends: median 3198, p90 4282, p95 6955 ms. Each send spawns a fresh claude: 906–1465 ms of process overhead outside the CLI's own duration_ms (median 1059), plus a median API time of 2079 ms
truth: engine = the user's Claude Code login, claude-sonnet-5 (from the CLI JSON); load 2.1-6.7

title: CH5: nothing streams: every reply appears whole after 2.2-7.0 s (0 incremental DOM updates in 14 replies) behind a fake 'reading the repo / thinking' ticker
repro: Send any message
Observe #msgs with a MutationObserver
expected: tokens appear incrementally, ≥ 5 DOM updates/s (B2.1)
actual: 1 DOM insert per reply, 0 updates after it. Before that, a canned ticker cycles every 1.8 s whatever is happening (it said 'thinking…' for the whole 90 s offline wait)

title: CH2/B1.5: an unavailable model costs a failed cold spawn (+1.5-1.7 s) on every send, silently falls back to claude-opus-5-5, and is never remembered
repro: Set the profile's model to an id this login can't use (here 'claude-unavailable-model-x')
Send two messages
expected: at most one extra round trip, the first time only, plus a note: '<model> isn't available on this login. Using <fallback> instead.'
actual: each send spawned with the bad model (failed after 1545 / 1665 ms: 'There's an issue with the selected model…'), then re-spawned on the CLI default. Answers came from claude-opus-5-5 with no note. First token 5090 / 4637 ms

title: CH4/B3.6: every chat send writes 0.9-1.8k tokens of prompt cache that is never read (cache_read 0 in 13/13 sends), roughly doubling cost per send
repro: Send 5+ messages in one conversation with the CLI JSON captured
Read usage.cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens
expected: ≥ 50 % cache reads from turn 3 (stable prefix first, live context last)
actual: cache_read_input_tokens 0 on every send; cache_creation 928-1780 on every send over ~1k tokens. Cost $0.0024 for the one sub-1k prompt, $0.0046-0.0076 for the rest. The live context (with the clock) sits before the conversation, so no prefix repeats

title: CH3/B1.4: Enter → claude spawn (context build + IPC) p95 217 ms (n=14, median 38 ms)
repro: Wrap the claude binary to timestamp its start
Compare with the Enter keydown timestamp, over 14 sends
actual: 23-217 ms; median 38, p95 217 (the first send of a fresh instance), next worst 106 ms

title: CH6/B2.4: Esc while a reply is pending closes the panel instead of stopping it; the request runs on and the answer pops up as a 140-char truncated bubble

Press Esc while 'reading the repo…' shows
expected: Esc (or a stop button) cancels within 200 ms, keeps the partial text marked 'stopped', and leaves the panel open
actual: the panel closes at once; the claude process keeps running. 3.3 s later the reply appears as a speech bubble cut to 'There's no agent named beacon in what I can see — just kestr…'. There is no stop control anywhere

title: CH11: no new chat, history list, search or clear: '/new' is 'Unknown command', ⌘N does nothing, Quick asks vanish after the first message until restart

title: CH15/CH16: offline and HTTP 429 both show 90 s of 'thinking…' then 'claude timed out'; the cause is never detected (on 429 the CLI was retrying every 23 s)
repro: Launch with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9 and send a message
Launch with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointing at a local server that returns 429 + retry-after: 23 + rate_limit_error JSON, and send
expected: offline: 'You're offline. I'll send this when you're back.' (queued). 429: 'Rate limited by Anthropic. Retrying in 23 s.' with a countdown and [Retry now]
actual: both: 'thinking…' for 90.0 s (90036 / 90068 ms), then 'That didn't work: claude timed out'. On 429 the server log shows POST /v1/messages at +0.6, +23.6, +46.6 and +69.7 s. The app's 90 s kill hid it; the CLI wrote nothing to stdout
truth: fault injection at the network boundary

title: CH14/B4.2: chat errors are raw strings with no action, and the failed message can't be retried (composer cleared)
repro: Launch with an invalid ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and send; or trigger the offline case above
expected: '<what happened>. <what to do>' plus one primary action (e.g. 'That API key was rejected… [Paste key]'), with the text kept in the composer or as a retryable message
actual: 'That didn't work: API key is invalid.' / 'That didn't work: invalid x-api-key' / 'That didn't work: claude timed out'. No button; the key form is not offered; the composer is empty; the user bubble has no retry

title: CH13: with no engine, the composer, messages and the whole command bar are hidden behind a key form; no install/login action; the header claims 'api key'

expected: 'I need a way to think. Paste an Anthropic API key, or install Claude Code and log in.' with [Paste key] [How to install]. Commands that need no model (/jump, /today, /goal) still work
actual: only the key form shows ('Chat uses your Claude Code login. No claude here? Paste an Anthropic API key…'), with focus in its password field. #chatForm, #msgs and the Quick asks are display:none, so /today goes into the key field. The header reads 'vibepet/main · api key' though no key exists
